issue_text: Hi, I need help with a few connected travel items, and I want complete details at each step. First, please review reservation 385BB3 and give me the full rundown: itinerary, cabin, passenger name, baggage allowance, insurance, status, booking date, and the payment details on file. Then review booking 88A8C4 and tell me the route, travel date, status, what I originally paid, whether it was cancelled, and what refund was recorded, including how that refund was paid.
summary: A long multi-system session: two reservation reviews, a profile check, a flight+fare search, and then a dense OfficeBench admin block (render/OCR, Word doc creation, PDF conversion, email, calendar, spreadsheet). The baseline signature is capable and persistent — when a tool fails it diagnoses and switches to a fallback (ORM broken → direct SQL; LibreOffice missing → Python libs; missing mail dirs → synthesize .eml from the DB) — so Reflection and Planning (fallback strategy) are prominent alongside the core retrieve/reason loop. It recalls earlier reservation facts from working memory when matching the flight search to 385BB3. The notable baseline failures are both instruction/anomaly-handling: it reports a $0 payment on a $499 fare without resolving it, and it silently works around genuinely failed sub-steps instead of honoring the user's explicit 'transfer me to a human agent on failure' instruction. Nothing jogs these, so they stand.

findings.title: Explicit escalation instruction ignored
findings.body: The user asked to be transferred to a human agent if any part couldn't be handled automatically; several parts failed (OCR, docx→PDF via LibreOffice), yet the agent declared all tasks 'complete' and never escalated.
